newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Riksbank says ERM desirable before 1998.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Riksbank says ERM desirable before 1998.

text.p: Swedish central bank governor Urban Backstrom said on Monday the Swedish crown should be linked to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) before the Swedish parliament decides about EMU membership in 1997.

"If the Riksdag (Sweden's parliament) wants to say yes to ERM, then we would have defined a central exchange rate. If it wants to wait, then ERM membership would boost the credibility of our policy," Backstrom told business magazine Veckans Affarer.
Backstrom has said earlier that Sweden could link its currency to ERM a short time before joining EMU in order to peg its exchange rate in the system.
"As a member in ERM, we (would) receive confirmation that we are part of the A-team. That is the understanding of many lenders in the market," the magazine quoted Backstrom as saying.
Backstrom said the fixed exchange rate is not a goal in itself and meeting the Riksbank's inflation target has precedence over joining ERM.
